parts.latex:
The size (in degrees, $d$) of each interior angle of a regular polygon with $n$ sides is given by the formula:

$$d=\dfrac{90(2n-4)}{n}$$

Use this formula to show that the size of each interior angle in a regular hexagon is $120^\circ$.

A stone is thrown straight up, and the height in metres after $t$ seconds is given by the formula

$$h = 9.8t - 4.9t^2 .$$

What is the stone's height when $t = 1$?

solutions.latex:
Substitute $t = 1$.
$$\begin{aligned} h &= 9.8(1) - 4.9(1)^2 \\ &= 4.9 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is B.

7200.stem:
The frequency ($F$) (number of vibrations per second) measured in Hertz, (Hz) of a string on a harp in relation to the length of the string (cm) can be modelled by the equation:

$$F = \dfrac{k}{\sqrt{L}} \qquad \text{where } k \text{ is a constant}$$

A string of length 25 cm on a harp has a frequency is 10 Hz.

parts.latex: Show that $k$ in the above equation has a value of 50.
What length of string would produce a frequency of 12.5 $Hz$ on the harp?

solutions.latex:
Substitute $L = 25$ and $F = 10$ into the formula.
$$\begin{aligned} 10 &= \dfrac{k}{\sqrt{25}} \\ k &= 10 \times 5 \\ &= 50 \end{aligned}$$

criteria: Correct substitution in the formula, or equivalent merit

7203.stem:
A square based pyramid with base edges of length $L$ cm and perpendicular height $h$ cm, is shown.

\exfigure{1265_q32_1}

The formulas for the volume ($V$) and surface area ($A$) of the pyramid in terms of $L$ and $h$ can be given by:

$$V = \dfrac{L^2 h}{3} \quad \text{and} \quad A = L^2 + L\sqrt{L^2 + 4h^2}$$

figures.cap: square based pyramid with base edge L and height h

parts.latex:
The pyramid has a surface area of 5184 cm$^2$ and its base area is 2304 cm$^2$.

Show that the perpendicular height of the pyramid is 18 cm.
What is the volume of this pyramid?

solutions.latex:
The base area is $L^2 = 2304$, so

$$L = \sqrt{2304} = 48$$

Substitute into the surface area formula $A = L^2 + L\sqrt{L^2 + 4h^2}$:

$$\begin{aligned} 5184 &= 2304 + 48\sqrt{2304 + 4h^2} \\ \dfrac{5184 - 2304}{48} &= \sqrt{2304 + 4h^2} \\ 60 &= \sqrt{2304 + 4h^2} \\ 3600 &= 2304 + 4h^2 \\ h^2 &= 324 \\ h &= 18 \end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore\ h = 18 \text{ cm}$$
criteria: Correct value of $L$, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source went from $\dfrac{5184-2304}{48}$ straight to $3600$ with a squaring step omitted; added the line $60=\sqrt{\cdots}$ (value $2880/48=60$, squared $3600$). Source has a figure \exfigure{1265_q32_1} in the question only.

solutions.latex:
Using $V = \dfrac{L^2 h}{3}$ with $L^2 = 2304$ and $h = 18$:

$$\begin{aligned} V &= \dfrac{2304 \times 18}{3} \\ &= 13\,824 \text{ cm}^3 \end{aligned}$$

7208.stem:
The acceleration due to gravity ($g$) of an object on a planet (measured in m/s$^2$) varies inversely with the square of the distance ($r$) that the object is from the centre of the planet.

For Earth, this relationship can be modelled by the formula: $g = \dfrac{4.0 \times 10^{14}}{r^2}$ where $r$ is in metres.

parts.latex:
The radius of Earth is approximately $6.4 \times 10^6$ metres.

Show by using the above formula, that the acceleration due to gravity on the Earth is approximately 9.8 m/s$^2$.

The acceleration due to gravity of a satellite orbiting the Earth is 0.02 m/s$^2$.

How far above the Earth's surface is the satellite? (Give your answer in standard form correct to one decimal place.)

solutions.latex:
Substitute $r = 6.4 \times 10^6$ into the given formula:

$$\begin{aligned} g &= \dfrac{4.0 \times 10^{14}}{(6.4 \times 10^6)^2} \\ &\approx 9.765 \\ &\approx 9.8 \text{ m/s}^2 \text{ (to 1 decimal place)} \end{aligned}$$

Substitute $g = 0.02$ into the formula to find the distance $r$ from the centre of the Earth:

$$\begin{aligned} 0.02 &= \dfrac{4.0 \times 10^{14}}{r^2} \\ r^2 &= \dfrac{4.0 \times 10^{14}}{0.02} = 2 \times 10^{16} \\ r &= 1.414\ldots \times 10^8 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

The height above the surface is $r$ minus the radius of the Earth:

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Distance} &= 1.414\ldots \times 10^8 - 6.4 \times 10^6 \\ &= 1.350\ldots \times 10^8 \\ &\approx 1.4 \times 10^8 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct value for $r$, or equivalent merit
Correct substitution in the formula, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
The price of a property purchased in 2021 was \$780 000.

The following table was used to calculate the stamp (transfer) duty paid on the purchase.

\exfigure{1264_q13_1}

The amount of stamp duty paid was

solutions.latex:
The price $\$780\,000$ lies in the band $\$310\,000$ to $\$1\,033\,000$, so the duty is $\$9285$ plus $\$4.50$ for every $\$100$ over $\$310\,000$.

The amount over $\$310\,000$ is
$$780\,000 - 310\,000 = 470\,000$$

This contains $\dfrac{470\,000}{100} = 4700$ hundreds.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Duty} &= 9285 + 4.50 \times 4700 \\ &= 9285 + 21\,150 \\ &= \$30\,435 \end{aligned}$$

This is option C.
